title: Kernel.system calls cause server to stop working
body: I am using gRPC 1.65.0 or newer with MRI Ruby 3.3.0 or newer on Linux, Linux containers, and macOS. If a server handler calls Kernel.system or executes a command with backticks, the current or following RPC is cancelled and the server stops accepting requests. I included a unit-test reproduction and a GRPC::Cancelled stack trace.

symptoms_visible: With gRPC 1.65.0 or newer and MRI Ruby 3.3.0 or newer, calling Kernel.system or using backticks inside a server handler causes a GRPC::Cancelled error and the server stops handling subsequent requests.
N0.label: N0 shell call stops Ruby gRPC server

symptoms_visible: If I put the shell call in another thread but wait for its result, the cancellation and server failure reappear.
N1_x.label: N1_x separate-thread workaround aftermath

symptoms_visible: In the minimal Greeter example, the first call returns its greeting but logs a GOAWAY that cancels calls; the second client call then fails with connection refused.
N2.label: N2 minimal Greeter reproduction supplied

symptoms_visible: The shell-call tests fail on Ruby 3.3 and 3.4 across Linux and macOS, while I cannot reproduce the failure on Ruby 3.1 or 3.2.
N3.label: N3 Ruby-version boundary confirmed

symptoms_visible: On the source-built development gem containing the fix, the functional tests that previously failed after Kernel.system calls now pass on Ruby 3.3 and 3.4, and the same build also works on Ruby 3.1 and 3.2.
N_terminal.label: terminal fix verified by affected user

solution.intent: Run Kernel.system in a separate Ruby thread so the RPC-handling thread is not blocked.
solution.concrete_example: Wrap Kernel.system(command) in Thread.new and let it execute in the background rather than blocking the RPC handler.

edges.comment: From c0-c1: participant1 suggested a separate thread; the reporter explained that it only appears to work when no result is needed and that synchronizing with the thread makes the failure reappear on the reporter's system.

question_patterns: Can you provide a minimal reproduction using the Ruby Greeter example?
Please show the smallest server handler that reproduces the problem and what happens on consecutive client calls.
clarifications.user_answer_in_this_oncall: I can reproduce it with the standard Greeter server by adding Kernel.system('echo "test"') inside say_hello. The first client call prints "Greeting: Hello world" but also logs a GOAWAY with "Cancelling all calls". On gRPC 1.69.0, the second call fails with connection refused. I attached a screenshot. I also had to recompile the example proto files because the checked-in helloworld_pb.rb raised an undefined-method error with these versions.

counterfactual_candidates.answer: The minimal Greeter example continues accepting repeated calls after Kernel.system; I can reproduce the cancellation only in my full application.
The first call succeeds and the third rather than the second call gets connection refused, with the same GOAWAY immediately after the shell call.

edges.comment: From c2-c3, describing the reporter's system: participant2 requested a simple reproduction after an initial non-reproduction, and the reporter supplied the Greeter handler, consecutive-call output, proto-regeneration note, and screenshot.

question_patterns: Which exact Ruby versions reproduce this, and which versions do not?
Can you retest the reproduction on Ruby 3.1, 3.2, 3.3, and 3.4?
clarifications.user_answer_in_this_oncall: I checked again and cannot reproduce it on Ruby 3.1 or 3.2; my earlier 3.1 claim was mistaken. Across our affected Linux and macOS setups, it reproduces on Ruby 3.3 and 3.4.

counterfactual_candidates.answer: It reproduces identically on Ruby 3.1 through 3.4, including with gRPC versions older than 1.65.
Ruby 3.3 and 3.4 reproduce it on Linux; Ruby 3.1 and 3.2 remain unaffected, but I have not rerun every version on macOS.

edges.comment: From c4-c5 and c8: participant3 reported the same failure on Ruby 3.3/3.4 but not older Rubies, participant2 reproduced on 3.4 but not 3.2, and the original reporter corrected the opening claim after retesting. The affected users are folded into one simulated user side.

solution.intent: Fix the Ruby gRPC extension's shutdown behavior by removing the obsolete channel polling thread and restoring timer-based completion-queue polling, so a subprocess-related invocation of Ruby's unblocking callback cannot shut down the server.
solution.concrete_example: With Event Engine enabled, remove the no-longer-needed channel polling thread and return that path to the earlier timer-based completion-queue polling behavior. The merged development build was then tested successfully with Kernel.system on Ruby 3.3 and 3.4, while remaining compatible with Ruby 3.1 and 3.2.
solution.inference_hint: The reporter supplied the shell-call reproduction and Ruby-version boundary. Engineers connected that evidence to the gRPC extension's rb_thread_call_without_gvl unblocking callback, which had been changed to initiate shutdown, and concluded that removing the obsolete channel polling thread and restoring timer-based polling was the appropriate fix.

edges.comment: Technical chain from c5, c13-c16: participant2 first connected shelling out on newer Ruby to an unblocking callback that could initiate shutdown, then implemented the Event Engine-compatible removal of the polling thread and restoration of timer-based polling. Terminal verification comes from c20: participant3, an affected user from c4, tested the already-merged source development build on their own functional tests across Ruby 3.1-3.4.

solution.intent: Fix the Ruby gRPC extension's shutdown behavior by removing the obsolete channel polling thread and restoring timer-based completion-queue polling, so a subprocess-related invocation of Ruby's unblocking callback cannot shut down the server.
solution.concrete_example: Update to a build containing the Ruby extension change that removes the obsolete channel polling thread and restores timer-based completion-queue polling, then rerun consecutive RPCs whose handler waits for Kernel.system.
solution.inference_hint: This shortcut represents proposing the ultimately accepted gRPC runtime fix immediately from the opening report. It skips the later minimal reproduction, version-matrix testing, and falsification of the separate-thread workaround.

edges.comment: Answer-key shortcut required because the thread's first proposed move was the falsified separate-thread workaround. It reaches the same merged fix and affected-user verification while explicitly recording the diagnostic evidence it skips.

satisfaction_conditions: Must identify the accepted root cause: on newer Ruby versions, subprocess activity can invoke the rb_thread_call_without_gvl unblocking callback, and the affected gRPC Ruby polling path had made that callback initiate server shutdown.
Diagnosis must be grounded in the minimal Greeter behavior and Ruby-version boundary: the first call logs GOAWAY, the next is refused, and the issue reproduces on Ruby 3.3/3.4 but not 3.1/3.2.
The durable fix must remove the obsolete channel polling thread and restore timer-based completion-queue polling under Event Engine rather than requiring application handlers to remove Kernel.system.
Must not present an unsynchronized background Thread.new call as the complete fix, because waiting for the shell result reproduces the failure.
Must ask an affected user to verify consecutive shell-calling RPCs on a build containing the fix and must not declare resolution until that verification succeeds.

persona_hint.experience_level: Experienced Ruby developer who can modify and rebuild gRPC examples, regenerate protobuf files, test multiple Ruby and gem versions, and provide exact client and server output.
persona_hint.communication_style: Polite, cooperative, and evidence-oriented; supplies runnable code and logs, corrects earlier version claims after retesting, and clearly explains constraints that prevent application-level workarounds.
